newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-CALCAVECCHIA ON RECORD PACE IN LEADING BOB HOPE CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-CALCAVECCHIA ON RECORD PACE IN LEADING BOB HOPE CLASSIC.

text.p: Mark Calcavecchia shot an eight-under-par 64 Saturday to equal the PGA Tour's 72-hole record and grab a three-stroke lead with one round to play at the Bob Hope Chrysler Classic.
Calcavecchia stood at 27-under-par 261 after his round at Bermuda Dunes, a total that equalled the tour's 72-hold record set by Ben Hogan in 1945 and matched by Mike Souchak in 1955.
The five-round event, played on four different courses, concludes Sunday with all players competing at Indian Wells.
Second place was held by John Cook, who fired a 10-under 62 for 264, three shots better than Don Pooley. John Daly was tied for fourth with Mark O'Meara at 268.

Said Calcavecchia of his record scoring spree: "Actually, I'm kind of impressed. In October I shot 26-under the last four rounds in Las Vegas (another 90-hole event) and thought I'd never accomplish that again. But here I am at 27 under. That's pretty good, I think."
Calcavecchia needs to shoot 64 in the final round to tie the tour's 90-hole mark, set at the Hope in 1993 by Tom Kite.

Calcavecchia birdied the last four holes, the first of that series a recovery from a tee shot which hooked to within two yards of out of bounds. He had five other birdies, as well as one bogey, the result of another bad drive.

John Cook had a bogey among his 11 birdies at Indian Wells. The bogey came on the 13th hole, when he failed to get up and down from a bunker, but Cook recovered well after losing that stroke, carding birdies on the next five holes.

"It's awfully early in the year to be shooting 62s, but I got off to a good start and it flowed from there," said Cook. "After making six birdies on the front, I figured I'd come to a screeching halt, but I kept it going."
Daly is in contention for the first time since the Kemper Open last June. He says that some credit for his improved play belongs to Tiger Woods.
"Tiger's taken a lot of the heat and the pressure off of me, but he's made me hungrier to come out and do better. I think he's made the whole tour rise to the occasion."
